rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic expression is uniquely elevated and sublime; its eloquence astonished the Arabs, who could not produce anything comparable.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف بين أهل العلم أن التعبير القرآني تعبير فريد في عُلُوِّهِ وسُمُوِّهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge escalated from ten fabricated surahs to one surah, then declared that all humans and jinn together could never match the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: تحداهم أولاً بأن يأتوا بعشر سور مثله إن كانوا يرون أنه مفترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one-surah challenge includes short as well as long surahs; Arabs knew they could not answer it and found war and coalition-building easier.
rows.anchor: ويشمل هذا التحدي قِصارَ السور كما يشمل طوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquence so affected hearers that opponents tried to stop people listening, since merely hearing it shook the soul powerfully.
rows.anchor: مجرد وصوله إلى السمع يُحْدِثُ في النفس دَويّاً هائلاً وهِزَّة عنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, and al-Akhnas secretly listened to the Prophet recite for three nights, then repeatedly vowed not to return.
rows.anchor: أبي جهل وأبي سفيان والأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: After rejecting labels such as poet, soothsayer, sorcerer, and madman, al-Walid praised the Qur’an’s sweetness, beauty, and superiority.
rows.anchor: قول الوليد بن المغيرة بِسِرٍّ. فقد اجتمع إليه نفر من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic expression is deliberate at the level of every word and letter; placement considers the whole Qur’an, not only an individual verse or surah.
rows.anchor: كل لفظة بل كل حرف فيه وُضِعَ وضعاً فنياً مقصوداً

rows.speaker: ملاك التأويل
rows.claim: Early scholars observed that disconnected-letter surahs often repeat their opening letter in their words; the book argues this by comparing similarly sized surahs.
rows.anchor: إن هذه السور إنما وقع في أول كل سورة منها ما كثر تَردادهُ فيما تركب من كَلِمها

rows.speaker: ملاك التأويل
rows.claim: As a statistical example, Yunus contains about 220 words built on rāʾ, while the nearest non-initial-letter comparator, al-Nahl, has about 200 despite being longer.
rows.anchor: تكرر في سورة يونس من الكلام الواقع فيها الراء مائتا كلمة وعشرون كلمة أو نحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourteen disconnected letters are half the alphabet and occur across 29 surahs; together they include half of numerous phonetic letter classes.
rows.anchor: أن عدد هذه الحروف أربعة عشر حرفاً أي بمقدار نصف حروف المعجم ترددت في تسع وعشرين سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites word-count symmetry: al-dunya and al-ākhirah each occur 115 times, angels and devils 88, and death and life (with derivatives) 145.
rows.anchor: أن (الدنيا) تكررت في القرآن بقدر (الآخرة) فقد تكرر كُلُّ منهما 115 مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further counts pair summer and heat with winter and cold five times, and bad deeds with good deeds (including derivatives) 167 times.
rows.anchor: وأن (الصيف) والحر تكررا قدر لفظ (الشتاء) والبرد فقد تكرر كل منهما خمس مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also pairs kufr with īmān 17 times, kufran with īmānan eight times, and Iblis with the term for seeking refuge 11 times.
rows.anchor: وأن لفظ (الكفر) تكرر بقدر لفظ (الإيمان) فقد تكرر كل منهما 17 مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other asserted count matches pair al-kāfirūn with fire and war with captives; qālū and the command qul each occur 332 times.
rows.anchor: وأن لفظ (قالوا) تكرر 332 مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular word for month occurs 12 times, singular day 365 times, and plural days 30 times, corresponding to calendar counts.
rows.anchor: وأن لفظ (الشهر) تكرر 12 مرة بعدد الشهور السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the singular/plural count pattern through Arabic usage: plural forms mark paucity (three to ten), while singular forms can mark large quantities.
rows.anchor: تستعمل الجمع تمييزا لأقل العدد وهو ثلاثة إلى عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He extends the rule to adjectives: a plural adjective suggests fewer described objects, while a singular adjective suggests many.
rows.anchor: فالوصف بالمفرد يدل على الكثرة، والوصف بالجمع يدل على القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singular verb agreement can indicate many spears and feminine plural agreement few; he illustrates the pattern in 9:36 with منها for twelve months and فيهن for four sacred months.
rows.anchor: لما قال: (أربعة) قال: (فيهن)

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that the Qur’an’s wonders never run out and it does not grow stale through repeated recitation.
rows.anchor: لا تنقضي عجائبه ولا يَخلَقُ من كثرة الرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the Qur’an uses plural الرياح for winds bringing good and mercy, but singular الريح for evil and punishment.
rows.anchor: استعمل (الرياح) حيث وردت في القرآن الكريم في الخير والرحمة، واستعمل (الريح) في الشر والعقوبات

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf offers two senses for humility toward believers: it connotes tenderness and affection, or depicts people of high rank lowering their wings to believers.
rows.anchor: أن يُضَمِّنَ الذلَّ معنى الحُنُوِّ والعطف كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Despite their honor and elevated rank, these people lower their wings toward believers, explaining the expression أذلة للمؤمنين.
rows.anchor: مع شرفهم وعلو طبقتهم وفضلهم على المؤمنين خافضون لهم أجنحتهم

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 34:24, على presents the guided as elevated and firmly established, whereas في portrays the misguided as fallen or immersed; other verses consistently use these prepositions this way.
rows.anchor: استعمل مع الهداية حرف الاستعلاء (على) ومع الضلال (في)

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf pictures the person with truth riding a fine horse at will, while the misguided person is submerged and lost in darkness.
rows.anchor: لأن صاحب الحق كأنه مستعلٍ على فرس جواد يركضه حيث يشاء

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Al-Tafsīr al-Qayyim says على conveys the believer’s elevation through truth, firmness, and uprightness on the path, nuances not carried by إلى.
rows.anchor: ما يدل على علوه وثبوته واستقامته

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: By contrast, في for error, doubt, and darkness depicts a person immersed and entangled within them.
rows.anchor: الدال على انغماس صاحبه وانقماعه وتدسسه فيه

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path of truth rises with its traveler toward God Most High, whereas the path of error descends with its follower toward the lowest depths.
rows.anchor: فإن طريق الحق تأخذ علواً صاعدة بصاحبها إلى العلي الكبير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes على in the verse about defrauders as equivalent to من (“from”).
rows.anchor: إنّ (على) هنا بمعنى (من)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the sense of domination and control over people, rather than treating على as a synonym of من.
rows.anchor: بل هو متضمن معنى التسلط على الناس والتحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اكتال منه need not imply taking an unfair amount, but اكتال عليه signals domination; this suits defrauders who take extra and give less, making على more forceful than من.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه معنى التسلط والاستعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting لام in “كالُوهم/وزنوهم” rather than saying “لهم” signals that the defrauders withhold what is due, since لام denotes entitlement.
rows.anchor: اللام تفيد الاستحقاق وهم لم يعطوهم حقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the preposition after ترغبون deliberately leaves both رغبة فيهن and رغبة عنهن possible: guardians may desire beautiful orphan women or shun unattractive ones, under the same ruling.
rows.anchor: لأنه يراد معنى الحرفين معاً

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains the omitted preposition as permitting “desire to marry them” for their beauty or “turn away from marrying them” for unattractiveness.
rows.anchor: يحتمل في {أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ} [النساء: 127] لجمالهن

rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: Durra al-Tanzil explains أنزل إلينا in 2:136 because Muslims receive revelation at its endpoint through prophets, while أنزل علينا in 3:84 suits the Prophet, to whom it was revealed.
rows.anchor: فالمؤمنون لم ينزل الوحي في الحقيقة عليهم من السماء، وإنما أنزل على الأنبياء ثم انتهى من عندهم إليهم

rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: Durra al-Tanzil attributes the repeated أُوتِيَ in 2:136 to the preceding covenant passage, which already mentions being given scripture and wisdom, so Aal Imran need not repeat it.
rows.anchor: إنما اختص هناك لأن العشر التي فيها مصدرة بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that Baqara recounts earlier prophets and their stories, so repeating the statement that they were given revelation suits its context.
rows.anchor: الآية في سورة البقرة جاءت في سياق ذكر عدد من الأنبياء وأخبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because 2:135 has just mentioned Jews and Christians, Baqara appropriately singles out what Moses and Jesus were given before mentioning the other prophets.
rows.anchor: فلما جرى ذكر هاتين الملتين ناسب ذلك تخصيص نبييهما بالإيتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aal Imran follows the covenant concerning belief in and support for Muhammad, then stresses Islam as the accepted faith; the context centers on Muhammad’s message, so it does not repeat the gift formula for earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه لما كان السياق في البقرة في ذكر الأنبياء ذكر الإيتاء لهم
